title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Jayden Reed (neck) ruled out
items.desc: The Packers have ruled out WR Jayden Reed for the remainder of Week 2 with a neck injury.
items.impact: Reed was carted off the field on the Packers' second play of the day. The Packers will rely on Christian Watson and Matthew Golden as the two primary wide receivers for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Jets.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: A.J. Terrell Jr. (groin) doubtful to return
items.desc: Falcons CB A.J. Terrell Jr. (groin) is listed as doubtful to return Sunday.
items.impact: Terrell was originally evaluated for a concussion and was cleared, but also suffered a groin injury prior to leaving the game. The Falcons appear to be without their best defender in their secondary for the remainder of Week 2.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Saquon Barkley (stinger) questionable to return Sunday
items.desc: Saquon Barkley (stinger) is questionable to return for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Tennessee Titans Sunday according to Mike Garafolo.
items.impact: Barkley suffered the injury early in the first quarter for the Eagles, with Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley taking over the backfield for head coach Nick Sirianni against the Titans.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Ronnie Stanley (toe) active for Week 2
items.desc: Ronnie Stanley (toe) is active for Week 2 for the Baltimore Ravens against the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: Stanley is good to go after practicing late in the week while carrying a questionable designation, providing a boost to a Baltimore offensive line that will look to establish their elite ground game early in the Week 2 contest against the Saints.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Trey Hendrickson (finger) active for Week 2
items.desc: Trey Hendrickson (finger) is active for Week 2 for the Baltimore Ravens against the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: Hendrickson will suit up and play with a cast on the injured hand, boosting a Baltimore defensive line that will look to disrupt New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough early and often in the Week 2 matchup.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Blake Cashman (wrist) active for Week 2
items.desc: Blake Cashman (wrist) is active for Week 2 for the Minnesota Vikings against the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Cashman will suit up after progressing throughout the week managing the injured wrist, boosting a Minnesota defense tasked with attempting to slow down a high-powered Bears offense in the divisional matchup.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Andrew Van Ginkel (chest) active for Week 2
items.desc: Andrew Van Ginkel (chest) is active for Week 2 for the Minnesota Vikings against the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Van Ginkel passed through pregame activities without any issues, boosting a Minnesota defense that will look to contain a high-powered Bears offense in the divisional clash Sunday.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) officially inactive for Week 2
items.desc: Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) is officially inactive for Week 2.
items.impact: Tagovailoa was considered doubtful to play Sunday against the Panthers. Cooper Rush will draw his second straight start, with Jack Strand serving as QB2 for the Falcons.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Brian O'Neill (knee) active for Week 2
items.desc: Brian O'Neill (knee) is active for Week 2 for the Minnesota Vikings against the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: O'Neill will suit up after not suffering any setbacks during pregame warmups, boosting a Minnesota offensive line that will look to keep quarterback Carson Wentz upright against an aggressive Chicago defensive front Sunday.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Chris Olave (hamstring) officially active for Week 2
items.desc: Saints WR Chris Olave (hamstring) is officially active for a Week 2 matchup with the Ravens.
items.impact: Olave was a late addition to the injury report this week and was listed as questionable to play in Week 2. He immediately becomes the top pass catching option for QB Tyler Shough and the Saints.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Sean Tucker (hamstring) officially active for Week 2
items.desc: Buccaneers RB Sean Tucker (hamstring) is officially active for Week 2.
items.impact: Tucker was forced to sit out Week 1 due to a hamstring injury. He should mix into the running back rotation with Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell against Cleveland.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Tyson Campbell (ankle) officially active for Week 2
items.desc: Browns DB Tyson Campbell (ankle) is officially active for Week 2.
items.impact: Campbell was listed a questionable to play against Tampa Bay, but he will suit up for the Browns in Week 2. This gives the Browns' defense Campbell and Denzel Ward to deal with Tampa Bay's WR group.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Lukas Van Ness (concussion) active for Week 2
items.desc: Lukas Van Ness (concussion) is active for Week 2 for the Green Bay Packers against the New York Jets.
items.impact: Van Ness was able to clear through concussion protocols throughout the week to get the green light Sunday, boosting a Green Bay defensive front that will look to put pressure on Jets signal caller Geno Smith early and often in the Week 2 matchup.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Jalen McMillan (knee) officially active for Week 2
items.desc: Buccaneers WR Jalen McMillan (knee) is officially active for Week 2.
items.impact: McMillan has been dealing with a knee injury dating back to the offseason and is expected to be on a snap count this week. Fantasy managers should likely find another option until McMillan is 100%.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) active for Week 2
items.desc: Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) is active for Week 2 for the Green Bay Packers against the New York Jets.
items.impact: Bako-Bewele is good to go after passing through pregame activities without any issues, joining Aaron Banks (knee) to boost a Green Bay offensive line after a forgettable Week 1 performance.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Aaron Banks (knee) active for Week 2
items.desc: Aaron Banks (knee) is active for Week 2 for the Green Bay Packers against the New York Jets.
items.impact: Banks will suit up after entering the weekend carrying a questionable designation, boosting a Green Bay offensive line that will look to put a dismal Week 1 performance in the rearview mirror against the Jets Sunday.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: D'Angelo Ponds officially inactive for Week 2
items.desc: Jets CB D'Angelo Ponds is officially inactive for the Jets' Week 2 matchup with Green Bay.
items.impact: Ponds was rumored to make his 2026 debut this week, but is a healthy scratch this weekend. He will have to wait at least one more week before making his debut.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Kendre Miller officially inactive for Week 2
items.desc: Saints RB Kendre Miller is officially inactive for the Saints' Week 2 matchup with Baltimore.
items.impact: Miller was not listed on the injury report this week and is a healthy inactive. Alvin Kamara (knee) makes his return to the lineup for the Saints.

items.author: Jesse Garcia
items.title: Joe Burrow (back) will start Sunday
items.desc: Bengals QB Joe Burrow (back) will start for the Bengals in their Week 2 matchup with the Texans.
items.impact: Head coach Zac Taylor stated that "he feels good" and is "ready to go." Fantasy managers should expect Burrow to not be limited in his play Sunday, barring him reaggravating his back injury.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Brock Bowers (knee) not expected to play Sunday
items.desc: Brock Bowers (knee) is not expected to play in Week 2 for the Las Vegas Raiders against the Los Angeles Chargers according to Ian Rapoport.
items.impact: Bowers could return as soon as Week 3 for the Raiders according to Rapoport, with Michael Mayer in line for increased touches again in Week 2 against the Chargers.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Sam Darnold (glute) progressing quicker than expected
items.desc: Sam Darnold (glute) is progressing quicker than expected from his Week 1 injury for the Seattle Seahawks according to Ian Rapoport.
items.impact: Darnold has made significant progress in hopes of returning sooner than late for the Seahawks, remaining week-to-week currently. Drew Lock will continue to start behind center in his absence.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Chris Jones (calf) expected to play Sunday
items.desc: Chris Jones (calf) is expected to play for the Kansas City Chiefs against the Indianapolis Colts Sunday night according to Ian Rapoport.
items.impact: Jones will test the injured calf during pregame activities for the Chiefs and barring any setbacks will offer head coach Andy Reid a disruptive interior option against an Indianapolis offense that will likely attempt to establish the run early with Star running back Jonathan Taylor Sunday night.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Michael Penix Jr. (knee) could make his debut Thursday against Packers
items.desc: Michael Penix Jr. (knee) is nearing a return to play and could make his debut next Thursday against the Packers.
items.impact: The Falcons will be starting Cooper Rush once again in Week 2, but Penix's return to the lineup would be a big boost to the Falcons' pass catchers. Penix has been edging ever closer to returning, and despite Tua Tagovailoa being named starter by default, he will likely start as soon as he is physically able.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: RJ Harvey (hamstring) unlikely to play against Jags
items.desc: RJ Harvey (hamstring) is unlikely to play against the Jaguars on Sunday due to a hamstring injury.
items.impact: If Harvey sits, JK Dobbins will once again be the primary rusher and it will open up touches for Jonah Coleman, as he is a capable pass catcher. Dobbins is worth starting this week, and Coleman could be an interesting start in deeper formats.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Kaelon Black (groin) expected to play on Sunday
items.desc: Kaelon Black (groin) is expected to play on Sunday against the Dolphins.
items.impact: If Black plays it seems unlikely he'll have the 50-50 split with Christian McCaffrey he had last time out, and likely will play a more complementary role. However, if the Niners do get up big, he could see a decent amount of touches, so he could be flex-worthy in deep formats.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Ladd McConkey (ribs) pushing to play Sunday
items.desc: Ladd McConkey (ribs) is pushing to play on Sunday against the Raiders despite a cracked rib. There is optimism that he will play, as the team did not elevate a wide receiver from the practice squad this week. If he plays, he will be wearing a flak jacket.
items.impact: If Ladd goes, it's hard to imagine sitting him given how important he is to this offense. Tre Harris and Quentin Johnston could get some additional work, but Ladd will be the main man in town if active.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Greg Newsome II (rib) practices in full
items.desc: Greg Newsome II (rib) was a full participant at Saturday's practice session.
items.impact: Newsome has been limited by a rib injury at practice earlier this week, but he was a full go Saturday and carries no injury designation for Monday's matchup with the Rams.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Zay Flowers (hamstring) out against Saints
items.desc: Zay Flowers (hamstring) has been downgraded to out against the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: With Flowers out, Mark Andrews will become the primary target for Lamar Jackson. Rashod Bateman will be the Ravens top receiver on the depth chart, but it would be extremely hard to start him, given the amount of routes he run for just one target last week. Rookie Elijah Sarratt could be an interesting watch if called up, but it's best to start Andrews and move on.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Eddy Pineiro (illness) ready to go for Sunday's game
items.desc: Eddy Pineiro (illness) will kick for the 49ers in Week 2's matchup with the Dolphins.
items.impact: Pineiro has missed practice all week due to being under the weather, but the veteran kicker will be ready to go Sunday. Pineiro hit 2-of-3 field goals and all three of his PATs in Week 1.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Lewis Bond elevated for Week 2
items.desc: Lewis Bond has been elevated to the Texans' roster for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
items.impact: A sixth-round pick for the Texans in this year's draft, Bond is set to make his NFL debut when he steps on the field Sunday. The Texans are lacking some depth at wide receiver right now, with go-to guy Nico Collins (hamstring) ruled out.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Javon Hargrave (knee, concussion) will not play Sunday
items.desc: Javon Hargrave (knee, concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday.
items.impact: Hargrave will not be available for Sunday's matchup with the Jets, as he is dealing with multiple issues. Jonathan Ford and Chris McClellan will likely see more snaps on defense.

items.author: Nate Miller
items.title: Carlton Davis III (neck) won't play Sunday
items.desc: Carlton Davis III (neck) will not be available for Week 2's matchup against the Steelers.
items.impact: Davis did not practice this week due to a neck issue. The veteran corner will take a seat on Sunday, as Charles Woods will likely step into more snaps on defense. Davis will try to be back for Week 3.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Puka Nacua (hip) questionable for Monday night
items.desc: Puka Nacua (hip) did not practice on Saturday and is now labeled questionable for Monday night against the Giants.
items.impact: Nacua has now missed two practices in a row with a hip issue, and that does not bode well for his status on game day. Fantasy managers will need to have contingency plans ready in case he sits. Davante Adams is next up for targets, but Colby Parkinson and Terrance Ferguson could see more looks. Konata Mumpfield is likely next up behind Puka with Jordan Whittington also questionable.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) ruled out Sunday
items.desc: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) has been ruled out for Week 2 for the Pittsburgh Steelers according to Mike Garafolo.
items.impact: Pittman Jr. will be sidelined after struggling to reach the practice field for head coach Mike McCarthy, with Roman Wilson and Germie Bernard in line for increased roles behind No. 1 wideout DK Metcalf against the Patriots Sunday.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) placed on injured reserve
items.desc: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) has been placed on injured reserve and will be sidelined for at least four weeks.
items.impact: The Jets are placing their first-round rookie on injured reserve after he suffered an ankle injury in his NFL debut last week. He is going to miss at least four weeks as a result, but he's not expected to be out much beyond that. Adonai Mitchell and Kenyon Sadiq will both see increased opportunities in his absence for the next few weeks at least.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kene Nwangwu (back) won't play Sunday
items.desc: Kene Nwangwu (back) won't play in Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: Nwangwu missed New York's season opener last week due to injury, and he is now set to miss another game on Sunday due to a back issue that he's dealing with. His absence won't have much of an impact on New York's offense, as he is relegated to more of a special teams role for the Jets.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Will McDonald IV (ankle) officially questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Will McDonald IV (ankle) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: McDonald will officially carry a questionable tag for Sunday's game after suffering a minor ankle injury during the week. It looks like he will be cleared to play in time, however, as HC Aaron Glenn told reporters that the veteran edge rusher should be available to play against the Packers.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Troy Franklin (knee) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Troy Franklin (knee) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
items.impact: Franklin found himself on the injury report earlier in the week due to a knee issue, but he was able to practice in full all week and will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant for the foreseeable future, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Marvin Mims Jr. (foot) unavailable for Sunday
items.desc: Marvin Mims Jr. (foot) will be unavailable for Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
items.impact: Mims is going to be sidelined in Week 2 after recently suffering a foot injury of some kind. He wasn't very involved on Denver's offense in the season opener, so his absence isn't expected to make much of an impact from a fantasy perspective.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) cleared to play Sunday
items.desc: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Thomas suffered a shoulder injury during the team's season opener last week, but he was able to practice all week and won't miss any time because of it. He has been cleared to play on Sunday and should continue to contribute in his usual capacity for the Jaguars for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cole Van Lanen (knee) off injury report for Sunday
items.desc: Cole Van Lanen (knee) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Van Lanen's knee injury is nothing more than a minor issue at this point and won't stop him from playing on Sunday. Jacksonville's offensive line should be at full strength in Week 2, which is good news ahead of a tough matchup against Denver's stout defensive front.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Foyesade Oluokun (wrist) will play Sunday
items.desc: Foyesade Oluokun (wrist) will play in Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Jacksonville has cleared Oluokun to play in their matchup against Denver on Sunday. That's good news for the team, as he is one of their key defenders and will be needed in what projects to be a close matchup in Week 2.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: LeQuint Allen Jr. (hip) set to play Sunday
items.desc: LeQuint Allen Jr. (hip) is set to play in Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: To no surprise, Allen has received full clearance and will again be available to play on Sunday. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to get much work behind Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. in this matchup, however.
